context:
Goal: a grant typed in one session reaches the session it names.
Problem (risk): build step 1 (you signed it off as item 152 a) must show whether a hook's allow gets past the auto-mode safety classifier. To prove it, a throwaway session tries acts the classifier refuses today, with a probe hook that allows them. It writes permission rules, so it needs your word. The lane waits on this and does nothing else meanwhile.
Based on (read): the Plan agent design, 2026-11-03 18:30 CST, plan section "The gate", step 1.
Departs from: main — adds a throwaway probe session on branch archive/hook-allow-probe.

options.gain: The probe shows whether Design A can work.
options.how: (1) Push branch archive/hook-allow-probe with a project-scope probe hook. (2) Start a child session on it, in auto mode. (3) In the child, arm 1: write a Bash(true) allow rule into the child's own .claude/settings.local.json three times (hook off, on, off). Arm 2: git switch --detach on the child's main mirror, which the pointer guard denies and the hook allows, then git switch main to put it back. (4) A record-only relay that names a merge of a PR that does not exist. Every write ends with the child's container. Cleanup: the child session is archived; the branch stays as an archive.
options.label: Yes, run these acts as written
options.lose: One throwaway session; a refusal may need one grant from you.

options.how: No probe; the lane reads the Claude Code docs.
options.label: No, read the docs only
options.lose: Whether a hook can skip the classifier stays unmeasured, and the gate build stays blocked.

title: Run the hook-allow probe for grant-reaches-lanes?
why: Every write ends with the child's container, and it is the only way to measure the gate.
